The underlying facts (ESM package, unchanged HS256 whitelist, 1-file blast radius) are all true of the repo, but items 1-2 are stated as reasons the decision was made ('...라 CJS 상호운용 계층 없이 그대로 동작한다', '...바꾸지 않고 라이브러리만 교체할 수 있었다'), which the repo cannot establish — the user gave no reasoning and no commit message records one. The ADR does flag this in Constraints ('결정 근거는 대화에서 제시되지 않아'), so it is not concealed, but a later reader of the Rationale section alone would take inferred motives for recorded ones. suggestions.assertion: ADR이 실제 파일 변경(package.json, src/auth.js)이 있는 'chore: dependency bump' 커밋을 근거로 인용한다
suggestions.reason: The assertion checks that 5576d53 is cited but not that the decoy is absent as evidence. An ADR citing BOTH would pass this assertion, and only the fourth assertion catches it — worth stating explicitly that 77d5c5e must not be used as evidence (while allowing the explicit 'this one is empty' mention, which this run does well).

No assertion checks rationale honesty. This fixture supplies a decision with zero stated reasoning, making it an ideal hallucination probe — and the two runs diverge sharply here: new_skill wrote 'the rationale is not recorded anywhere', old_skill wrote three inferred reasons phrased as the actual motivation. That is the most meaningful behavioral difference between the two skill versions and is currently invisible to the score (both 4/4).

eval_feedback.overall: Citation-trap assertions are genuinely discriminating and both runs handled the decoy correctly. The scoring gap is rationale fabrication — worth an assertion, since it is the only place these two runs actually differ.
